title: statking-gap-audit
universal_lens: The StatKing audit formalizes a high-dimensional data manifold where the legally usable active coverage subspace is strictly bounded by a sparse licensing operator. The core mathematical tension arises from projecting an expansive, 546-source seeded universe onto a restricted, contractually valid domain, requiring rigorous trust-weighted interpolation to maintain metric fidelity.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps this gap via conformal prediction sets over the missing-data regime. Source trust acts as a Bayesian prior weighting the 800 candidate records. When licensed tracking or PFF-like grades are absent, GSI dynamically inflates the conformal interval, ensuring the 10-second UX layer communicates exact epistemic uncertainty rather than hallucinated precision.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the audit defines a constrained state-transition graph. Valid game states require complete trench and pressure tensors; missing data creates absorbing null-states. The engine utilizes archetype scaffolding to approximate unobserved transitions, but strictly flags these paths with reduced confidence scores, preventing flawed situational reasoning in production backtesting.

primitives.name: Active Coverage Deficit Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Brutal audit - CRITICAL: active, legally usable data coverage remains smaller than the seeded source universe.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S_seeded: cardinality of raw sources (dimensionless); S_active: cardinality of legally usable sources (dimensionless); Gap: set difference (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: The seeded universe represents the theoretical maximum information bound, while legal constraints act as a hard truncation filter on the available feature space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when S_active approaches zero, causing total system failure, or when the distribution of S_active is highly biased toward low-value metrics, rendering the remaining data useless for high-fidelity modeling.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSI Conformal Missingness Kernel, which calculates the volume of the unobservable feature space relative to the training manifold.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of active records to candidate capacity (currently 800 / 500,000).

primitives.name: Ten-Second Trust Compression Layer
primitives.verbatim_quote: - HIGH: premium UX must explain trust, coverage, conflicts, and missing data in ten seconds.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: T_cognitive: cognitive load threshold (seconds); I_trust: mutual information of provenance signals (bits); Delta_t: time-to-comprehension (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: User comprehension of complex data provenance can be compressed into a scalar trust score without losing critical variance regarding data conflicts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the underlying data conflicts are non-linear or adversarial, making it mathematically impossible to compress the truthfulness of the dataset into a sub-10-second heuristic.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the GSE 'Data Confidence Storytelling' module, translating high-dimensional conflict resolution vectors into binary or ternary UI indicators.
layer2.telemetry: UX A/B test conversion rates on pages displaying explicit missing data warnings.

primitives.name: Historical Production Proof Scaffold
primitives.verbatim_quote: - MEDIUM: backtesting and model proof are scaffolded with fixtures and need historical production predictions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: M_fixture: synthetic model performance (dimensionless); M_prod: live historical prediction accuracy (dimensionless); E_gap: expected value divergence (dollars/utility)
primitives.assumptions: Fixtures provide a necessary but insufficient lower bound for model robustness; true validation requires exposure to the noisy, incomplete nature of historical production environments.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses if the fixture environment perfectly overfits to clean data, leading to catastrophic drawdowns when deployed against the fragmented reality of the active coverage subspace.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSI 'Proof Foundation', bridging the gap between unit-test style validation and out-of-sample conformal calibration on messy, real-world NFL data.
layer2.telemetry: Divergence between fixture win-rates and live backtested Sharpe ratios.

reasoning_traces.think:
The StatKing Gap Audit exposes a fundamental duality in quantitative sports intelligence: the tension between the theoretical completeness of a seeded data universe and the practical, legally constrained reality of active coverage. Mathematically, we begin with a high-dimensional vector space V representing 546 seeded sources and 500,000 candidate records. The 'brutal audit' identifies a projection operator P that maps V to a strict subspace U (active, legally usable data). Because dim(U) << dim(V), any model trained exclusively on U risks severe bias if the projection P is not uniformly random but instead structurally correlated with high-value features like tracking or PFF-like grades. To resolve this, we introduce a trust-weighted interpolation kernel K. This kernel operates on the 800 metric definitions, assigning higher weights to features residing entirely within U, while dynamically penalizing features that rely on the missing complement V \ U. The 'ten-second trust compression' is essentially the evaluation of the spectral norm of K, providing a rapid, scalar measure of how much the current query relies on imputed versus observed data. Furthermore, the transition from 'fixtures' to 'historical production predictions' represents a shift from evaluating models on the clean, noise-free manifold of synthetic data to the rugged, discontinuous landscape of real-world historical data. The audit mandates that our backtesting framework must explicitly simulate the missingness patterns defined by the coverage gap. If a model performs well on fixtures but fails under the stochastic masking induced by the legal coverage constraints, it suffers from a 'production proof' failure. Thus, the sovereign primitives derived here—Coverage Gap, Trust Compression, and Production Scaffold—form a cohesive mathematical framework for navigating the incomplete data reality of professional sports analytics, ensuring that the Galaxy Sports Engine never hallucinates certainty where only probabilistic bounds exist.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This audit lineage traces back to the foundational problems of missing data in econometrics, specifically the Rubin multiple imputation framework, but accelerated through modern conformal prediction. Historically, sports analytics relied on complete, albeit shallow, box-score datasets. The advent of granular tracking data introduced massive dimensionality, but also severe licensing fragmentation. The StatKing audit is the direct descendant of the 'garbage in, garbage out' theorem, formalized here as a rigorous requirement for explicit missingness telemetry in high-frequency decision engines.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the opposing agent is the sophisticated bettor or front-office analyst who intuitively senses when a model is 'hallucinating' due to missing data. They do not see the raw vectors; they see the output confidence. Our engine must model their skepticism. By exposing the 'coverage gap' and 'conflicts' in the UX, we align our epistemic state with theirs. We are not just predicting outcomes; we are communicating the structural integrity of our knowledge base. If we hide the fact that trenches data is missing, we violate the user's implicit contract of transparency, destroying trust faster than a bad prediction ever could.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical cross-layer veto must be implemented to prevent leakage from the 'seeded source universe' into the 'active coverage' models. If a model inadvertently uses a feature that is only available in the broader, unlicensed universe during training but masked during inference, it will exhibit catastrophic performance degradation. The veto condition is triggered when the correlation between a proposed feature and the missingness mask exceeds a strict epsilon threshold. Furthermore, we must veto any UX presentation that implies deterministic certainty (e.g., a single point estimate) when the underlying conformal interval width exceeds a predefined tolerance, forcing the system to default to a 'data insufficient' state rather than presenting a misleadingly precise number.
